Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 1243 PM EST Thu Nov 12 2026
 

- Rain showers accompany a cold front tracking north to south today.

- Gusty north wind peaks at 25 to 30 mph this afternoon.

- Lake effect rain/snow showers set up tonight through Saturday. 
Minor wet snow accumulations are likely across the Thumb, mainly 
near Saginaw Bay and the Port Huron vicinity.

&&

.AVIATION...

Surface trough continues to sink across lower MI maintaining 
scattered shower chances through late afternoon. Ceilings remain 
chaotic ranging from high IFR to lower VFR though the bulk of the 
area holds under MVFR skies into this evening. Lake effect showers, 
with some snow potentially mixing in, begin to develop late this 
evening leading to transient pockets of precip and minor vsby 
reductions. This is expected to transition into 2 dominant bands, 
one off Saginaw Bay and southern Lake Huron, by early Friday 
morning. Within the highest intensity positions of these bands most 
if not all snow would be the primary p-type. Currently, FNT/DET 
stand the best shot to be directly downwind so opted for prevailing 
snow mention- DET likely stays warm enough to allow for a mix rather 
than all snow. Driving lower level winds being to shift by Friday 
afternoon directing ongoing lake effect activity east of the 
terminal corridor towards the St Clair River/southern Ontario.

For DTW... Scattered rain shower chances persist through the 
remainder of the afternoon before drier conditions return for the 
evening. Some pockets of light rain are possible late evening, tied 
to developing lake effect, but low confidence that these track 
overhead. Main lake effect bands fully form by Friday morning with 
the closest favored more toward DET. That said, pieces of this 
activity could break off and reach DTW particularly late morning-
early afternoon. Temperatures would be warm enough to support a rain-
snow mix in this outcome with minimal if any accumulation. 

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* High for ceilings at or below 5,000 feet through Friday afternoon.

* High for p-type as rain through 06z tonight. Medium for rain-snow 
  with any precip after 06z into Friday afternoon.

&&
